body:
Greetings.
It appears that I have missed this WHATNOT meeting, but I would like to attend the next one (as an observer).
Has the procedure for joining WHATNOT/triage meetings changed since this issue was raised?

I might have chaired this meeting and forgot to post the notes. Apologies.

Pushing through patching, issues created
Discussing removing XSLT
Mason: raised a few weeks ago
.. lively conversation
.. want to see if views are affected
.. some pretty passionate use cases with real use cases
.. still in the camp of deprecating this
.. comments? Changed views?
Olli: haven’t changed my mind, still for removing.
Brian: curious, RSS feed makes it seem like it is used
… “subscribe in a new tab page” use case for RSS
… seems common
Mason: this should be done with <link rel> and not sending users XSLT directly
.. it is a real thing, but it’s a bit of an accidental use case
.. while it’s real we have a way around it
.. the danger to all users overcomes this corner case
Brian: to be clear, not in favor of keeping XSLT
Kieth: curious about why don’t we ship a polyfill of sort
.. can we switch it to a well maintained blob of sandboxed JS?
.. we have PDF.js and that soft of thing
.. is it possible to bake in a removable extension etc?
Mason: all of this technically possible.
.. the polyfill is not very well maintained
.. perhaps slightly more sandboxed
.. we have weaned users off for a couple of decades
Sideshowbarker: brigading on social media. I have not thing anything in the comments
.. that was new information, in our standards, or anything compelling
.. nothing like “oh wow we haven’t thought about that”.
.. by our norms, I don’t think anything come up that would change
.. OTOH given the amount of passion we’ll have to deal with some continued negative reactions
.. I don’t think this is a case where we’re out of touch
Keith: the only compelling thing was about running on embedded. For everyone else that seems like an acceptable tradeoff.
Daniel: is this about the authors using the polyfill or shipping it with browsers?
Mason: both of those were discussed. This is about having a polyfill served with the site, and embedded devices can include an extension.
Daniel: not sure it’s worth the effort to switch to something new
Emilio: the main opposition was “we cannot use the JS polyfill”
.. a browser extension could work
.. it’s probably not a massive blocker
.. I wonder if we could inject the script that way
Noam: XSLT in served XML top level is not a web platform feature but a browser feature
Keith: disabling JS is not an argument that should be considered
Daniel: 260000 have the noscript extension in firefox
Keith: that is selective per-site
Brian: agreeing with Keith and Emilio. We shouldn’t consider JS disabled as a motivation
Emilio: removing XSLT doesn’t necessarily mean we remove XSLT processing of top-level xML, just we remove the JS API
Noam: (said the same basically)
Anne: it’s not just a browser feature
Anne: e.g. it is observable with window.open
Emilio: I don’t think anybody objects to removing the XSLTProcessor API
Anne: not sure about that
Mason: the strong comments are in the XML processor
Mason: can we move this to stage 2?
Olli: fine with me, we should push this through
Keith: there is no spec yet
Mason: let’s call it stage 1 and I’ll ask for it to move to 2 once there is a PR up?
Brian: SGTM
Simon: SG
Mason: thanks for the discussion
AI: Mason to prepare a PR
—------------------
Joey: updates from Apple on #8189
Anne: no updates
—------------------
Alex: speaking about elementInternals
Alex: e.g. popovertarget, the author would have to create all the association
Alex: the proposal is to have elementInternals.type which would set up all of this
Alex: people had concerns about where we specify this attribute? Is it mutable?
Alex: thinking to move this to a static property
Emilio: why we don’t we do stuff like “extends HTMLButtonElement” 
Keith: Apple objected to this
Anne: the problem with customized built-ins is that you can’t use your own element names
Anne: the webkit standards position has a lot of this
Emilio: other than that it looks good
Emilio: it shouldn’t be mutable
Anne: I don’t remember why we had static for form associated
Keith: timing issues I think
Keith: static is preferable for things like this I think
… easy to typo this in ways that it would fail
Emilio: some of the arguments against extending built ins apply
Anne: you only have the conflict on custom elements that opted into being a button
.. it’s a different concern from a generic custom element
Keith: it would result in the same thing because consumers who will get the interesttarget from the default button vs. users that would implement their own
Keith: the way around is to have mixins, with an array of things
Alex: this is the second issue, where we want to actually expose the properties etc. of what it means to have a button
Alex: the idea is to have elementInternals and a very specific interface
Alex: back to Keith’s concern about behavior conflict
.. are you concerned about conflict for the author?
Emilio: less severe than a class extension.  
.. it would be a problem when people extend their own element
.. maybe it should be more piecemeal
Anne: what is the specific conflict?
Emilio: e.g. in the custom code, it seems like the popovertarget starts working automatically
Alex: we can also add a static “supportedAttributes” property that exposes things more granularly
Emilio: perhaps behavesLike should be an array, but this feels like it’s two layers?
Mason: we already recommend using data- attributes to not step on platform features
Emilio: it’s ok to step on those… do authors follow this?
.. it feels like it should be more like mixing and matching
.. it’s like extending the builtin element with a lower surface
Mason: that’s kind of the point though
… it’s the core use case
Emilio: not objecting, but it’s a gradient between customize built ins and possible caveats for this proposal.
Alex: does the static change make sense:
Noam: the questions here are a bit bigger picture
Keith: still problems with the design
Alex: how do you define this using mixins
Keith: have implicit behavior based on included mixins
Emilio: whatever approach we take here, making it static is probably good
Alex: please follow the explainer
Keith: anything here that’s more behavioral than attribute-based?
.. what are the other cases
Alex: we started with button. Didn’t explore the table element etc.
Keith: curious whether this design is restrictive to things that are not driven by attributes
.. e.g. buttons submit forms
Alex: we want these buttons to behave like the native button
Noam: experience with authoring this in a common library?
Dan: doing it in the platform guarantees the right ARIA stuff etc
AI: close the “static” issue, invite people to read the explainer etc. for the high level architecture.
